interest: This file illustrates the administrative handling of congressional inquiries regarding foreign social and economic systems during the New Deal era. It demonstrates American constituent interest in Japan's postal life insurance system (a major state-run micro-insurance and welfare institution) during a period of intense domestic debate over social security in the United States. Additionally, it reveals the routine interdepartmental coordination between the Department of State and the Department of Labor, as well as the commercial and informational reporting functions expected of American consular posts abroad.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) classified under decimal file 894.5064 (Economic Matters: Insurance: Japan: Life). It records correspondence from May 1935 concerning the Japanese Post Office Life Insurance System, initiated by United States Senator Royal S. Copeland on behalf of Charles W. Palomba, who sought a copy of a report on Japan's postal insurance system. The State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs noted that Palomba might obtain the report on loan from the Department of Labor, and offered to instruct the American Consulate at Tokyo to procure a copy if Palomba agreed to cover any incurred expenses.

subfiles.about: A Department of State List of Papers recording correspondence with Senator Royal S. Copeland regarding a constituent's request for a report on the Japanese Post Office Life Insurance System.
subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State List of Papers docket sheet (Form DS-46) recording incoming and outgoing correspondence from May 1935 regarding the Japanese Post Office Insurance System. U.S. Senator Royal S. Copeland forwarded a letter from Charles W. Palomba requesting a copy of an official report on the Japanese postal insurance system. The Department of State suggested that Palomba might obtain the report on loan from the Department of Labor, and indicated that it would instruct the American Consulate in Tokyo to procure a copy if Palomba authorized payment for any incurred charges.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Inquiry on Japanese Post Office Insurance System
